summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, malnutrition, and long QT syndrome, was admitted for nausea and vomiting lasting two days, possibly triggered by grapefruit ingestion or recent Bactrim use. He was found to have pre-renal acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine, which improved with IV fluids. A urine culture confirmed Proteus mirabilis infection, and he was treated with a full course of Bactrim. He developed a mild pruritic rash after a dose of ceftriaxone, which resolved with Benadryl. His nausea improved with Ativan and hydration, and he tolerated oral intake by discharge. He was discharged home with antibiotics, instructions to resume G-tube feeds, and plans for outpatient follow-up including urine testing and EKG for QT monitoring.
